pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has the CHECK and DEFAULT 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item(); test 'AC-2' asserts the labels.
Test 'AC-3' checks the filtered lists in id order.
Test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
Test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views.
Test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.
The code implements it, but the last commit ba1e9e5 ('Follow-up edits') removed 'AC-7:' from the test title. No test names AC-7 now, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits' by a bot, renamed the AC-7 test and dropped its 'AC-7' tag. The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and does not mention it. Under the naming rule, AC-7 now has no test naming it.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7' in the test title. Don't strip acceptance tags in follow-up commits.

findings.what: The PR claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit changed a test title and removed its AC-7 reference. The PR body also never mentions that final commit.
findings.fix: Correct the PR body, or revert the rename.

findings.what: No test shows that the traffic worker sends the query string of a route like '/?priority=high' to the app. The fake app now records the query, but nothing asserts it.
findings.fix: Add an assertion that a round requests '/?priority=high' with its query intact.

lenses.note: Spec present; decisions (existing items normal, only high and low labelled) are followed.
AC-7 is no longer named by any test after the final commit. The state-table rows each have a test in the 'states' describe block.
I did not run the tests, but they read as asserting behaviour. The AC-7 tag was removed.
README mentions the filter and the allowed values. It does not mention the 400 response or the labels, which is minor.
The query is parameterised and the priority value is whitelisted. Empty and unknown values give 400.
The title is HTML-escaped. The priority value is whitelisted before it is used in output or SQL.
Server-rendered minimal HTML, with no UI or style files in the diff.
No browser flow was demonstrated and the diff has no UI framework files.
The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing' claims are inaccurate given the last commit.
